responseText:
I can provide exact commands, but because this is a destructive change (removing access and disabling credentials) I need you to confirm the targets and principals before you run them.

Please confirm:
- Which systems do you want changed? (GitHub repo access, AWS IAM group, other?)
- Exact account names/usernames to remove on each system (GitHub username and AWS IAM username). Should I assume the identifier is "marcus" on both systems?
- Do you also want credentials revoked (AWS access keys, console login) and sessions invalidated, or only group membership / repo write permission removed?

Once you confirm the three items above I will give the exact commands to run and a one-line audit note. (Below are ready-to-run command templates you can use if those assumptions are correct — replace PROFILE/USERNAME where noted and run only after confirming.)

If GitHub repo access removal and AWS IAM group removal are desired and the username is marcus, here are concrete commands:

GitHub (remove collaborator from repo acme/billing-service)
- Using GH CLI (requires gh authenticated as org admin):
  gh api -X DELETE /repos/acme/billing-service/collaborators/marcus

AWS IAM (remove user from group prod-deployers and revoke credentials)
- Remove from group:
  aws iam remove-user-from-group --group-name prod-deployers --user-name marcus --profile <ADMIN_AWS_PROFILE>
- Delete console login (removes console sign-in):
  aws iam delete-login-profile --user-name marcus --profile <ADMIN_AWS_PROFILE>
- List access keys:
  aws iam list-access-keys --user-name marcus --profile <ADMIN_AWS_PROFILE>
- For each access key ID returned, deactivate then delete (example for one key ACCESSKEYID):
  aws iam update-access-key --user-name marcus --access-key-id ACCESSKEYID --status
